name: unity-dev
description: Unity 6 game development skills for AI coding agents — forty-seven load-by-situation skills covering the loop from an empty project to a verified artifact.

plugins.name: unity-dev
plugins.description: Unity 6 game development, forty-seven load-by-situation skills covering the whole loop from an empty project to a verified artifact. Terminal & verification: unity-cli (the CLI's surface, exit codes that say whether a retry is honest, MCP wiring, the warm shell), unity-debug (CHECK THE INSTRUMENT FIRST — stale results files and settings assets that were never in effect; four loops, the fastest driving a LIVE Editor in sub-second round trips against ~20 s for batchmode; Safe Mode's deadlock), unity-play-harness (build the game so an agent can drive and read it — a one-line probe snapshot readable from a live Editor, Editor.log or a PlayMode test; named situations that boot straight into a moment and wait on a readiness set instead of a sleep; journey tests that sample the probe into a timeline and assert invariants; a feel complaint turned into a repeatable test; velocity read from a delegate so a 2D body, a CharacterController or a grid mover reports through the same key, with 2D situation templates and a 2D never-inside-geometry invariant), unity-profiling (the work behind a slow or uneven frame as numbers an agent can compare across changes — ProfilerRecorder counters without the Profiler window, 90-frame windows with median/p95/worst, scheduled/completed/discarded work counters for streaming and pooling, and a before/after table; a driven run is not a hardware benchmark), unity-device-testing (acceptance on a REAL Android or iOS phone from a terminal — a probe scene that logs one tagged line per state change, an adb/devicectl driver that asserts on those lines and taps system dialogs by focus and rotation, a human asked for one physical action at a time and verified from the device, and exit codes that keep a real failure apart from a broken harness), unity-search (a 'find / where is / what references X' question turned into one Unity Search query — asset type filters, folders, labels, ref= relationships, scene component queries — written out before it runs, and opened in a live Editor when one is reachable; read-only, it never selects, moves or edits a result). Day one: unity-new-project (editor pinning, .meta/LFS, UPM deps pinned to annotated tags, IL2CPP/ARM64, asmdef boundaries, and the async/-quit deadlock that makes a headless package install exit 0 and install nothing), unity-game-brief (the first hour, before any Unity work: one line of idea into a one-page experience brief, the look locked with images, an architecture proposal derived from the stated constraints — simulation/presentation split, seeded generation, floating origin — readiness written as testable invariants, then ONE interaction the human can play and react to), unity-gameplay (START HERE for a gameplay request that names no perspective — fingerprints the project from its scenes and prefabs: 2D or 3D, projection, view, movement model, Cinemachine major; routes controls, camera, animation and verification to the skill owning each; genre recipes written as six constraints rather than labels, level metrics derived from the controller's numbers, production stages with exit checks). 3C — input, camera, character: unity-input (gameplay reads one struct, never a device — an actions asset with keyboard, gamepad and touch schemes, a reader that latches presses in Update and hands each to FixedUpdate once, input buffering, on-screen sticks, pointer and stick aim, grid steps with key repeat, rebinding saved as JSON, and a scripted source that drives the same funnel from a journey test), unity-camera (camera jitter is two clocks disagreeing — find them before touching damping; Cinemachine rigs for 2D follow with a room confiner, pixel-perfect follow, third-person orbit with deocclusion, first person and fixed posts, shake and blends, the 2.x to 3.x name table, a rig builder, a camera probe and a journey that proves a rig holds on every frame), unity-animation (the game owns the state and the Animator renders it, for 3D Humanoid and 2D frame-clip characters — one writer per parameter through a bridge, blend trees and sprite state graphs built from script, AnimationEvents and attack windows that survive interruption, override controllers, foot and hand IK, Timeline handover, root motion, and a journey proving the shown state follows the game). 2D world: unity-2d-controller (a platformer character asks physics where the ground is and is not simulated by it — rules and collision as two halves that never mix, a kinematic motor with slopes, one-way and moving platforms, coyote time, variable jump, dash and wall jump, gravity and jump velocity derived from apex height and time to apex, free top-down movement with aim split from move, cell steps shown as tweens, the Animator bridge, and journeys that prove apex, coyote and buffer), unity-physics-2d (Box2D answered in its own vocabulary, never a PhysX rule with a 2D suffix — a symptom-routed ladder, first match wins, for callbacks that never fire, tunnelling, casts that miss or hit the caster, bodies that sleep or jitter, composite and tilemap colliders and one-way platforms, with a two-sided debug probe and a read-only scene audit), unity-2d-rendering (draw order is four keys in a fixed priority and z is the last of them — sorting layer, Order in Layer, render queue, distance along the sort axis; SortingGroup, Y-sort for top-down, isometric and hex scenes, the Light2D that does nothing or turns everything black, shadow casters, normal maps, sprite masks, parallax layers, and a sorting audit that lists every tie), unity-2d-level (a level is data with invariants and the Tilemap is one renderer of it — a serialisable level of tile ids, spawn, gate, pickups and entities painted into a fixed stack of six Tilemap layers, runtime tile edits, rooms and doors, chunks stitched into an endless run, Tiled and LDtk import, SpriteShape terrain, seeded generation, and a validator that exits 1 on a pickup the jump cannot reach), unity-2d-grid (the cell map is the truth and the transform is an animation of it — board logic for tactics games and tile puzzles on rectangular, isometric and hexagonal grids as plain C# with no scene: hexagonal offset, axial and cube conversion for Unity's layout, movement range by flood, A* paths, lines of sight, one occupancy map, push rules, turn order, undo, pointer to cell), unity-2d-animation (a skeletal sprite is a mesh and costs like one — a PSB imported as a character rig, bones then geometry then weights in the Skinning Editor, SpriteSkin bindings and CPU or GPU deformation, Sprite Library skins and equipment swapped through SpriteResolver, IK Manager 2D limbs, and an audit of what a rig costs). UI: unity-game-ui (detects the project's UI system and routes; owns the runtime IMGUI HUD that editor-tooling docs never cover — GUI.matrix scaling, event swallowing, a type scale derived from viewing distance in arcminutes, mixed Latin/CJK font authoring), unity-ui-ugui (the six ways Canvas UI renders nothing, and the Layout Group vs ContentSizeFitter conflict), unity-ui-toolkit (USS is a subset of CSS and an unsupported property is ignored, not an error). Assets: unity-3d-models (inspect AI-generated GLB before Unity sees it and decimate what is over budget), unity-2d-sprites (sprite metadata lives in the importer; a set of frames turned into a playable AnimationClip; the capability gate that prevents silent corruption), unity-rigged-character (characters take the FBX route because glTFast cannot build an Avatar; bind-pose bounds make measured hitboxes arm-span wide), unity-2d-pixel-perfect (soft, crawling or seam-ridden pixel art, across both of the components called PixelPerfectCamera), unity-sprite-atlas (V2 atlases from script: the editor/runtime split, packing and platform settings, and how the packed texture reaches the player), unity-tilemap (Tile Palettes for rectangular, hexagonal and isometric grids, and RuleTiles generated from a terrain sheet you already have). Runtime domains: unity-physics-3d (symptom-routed triage, first-match-wins, a two-sided probe), unity-navigation (the agent owns the transform — decide that first), unity-render-urp (the Volume pre-flight behind 'I set it and nothing happened', the mobile subset, an eight-point Render Graph review), unity-urp-migration (a Built-in project moved to URP in five gated phases, each one read back from the saved project rather than from the converter log — magenta materials and the 2D shader hijack, PPv2 into a Volume profile that survives a reload, lightmaps that are still Built-in data, GrabPass/OnRenderImage/surface shaders, and the four traps that let a half-moved project look done), unity-audio (load types, sample rates, mixer cost; reports before it reimports), unity-localization (the CJK font pipeline, and the two contradictory standard answers for it). Shipping: unity-android-release (build it then PROVE it — a driver that refuses rather than warns, reading the artifact back with aapt/apksigner, per-build provenance), unity-web-release (the server headers that undo every Unity setting, and iOS Safari's memory ceiling), unity-ios-build (from a Unity project to a process on an iPhone without opening Xcode — headless build, an unsigned compile gate, signing with what the Mac actually holds and why the id in a certificate's name is not the team, devicectl install and the console as the only log channel, and a native .mm plugin iterated in 30 seconds instead of six minutes). Backend & commerce: unity-live-services, unity-monetization, unity-multiplayer, and the API layer they hand off to — unity-ugs (which package provides what, the initialisation order everything else depends on, Cloud Save access classes, Cloud Code, Remote Config, the Deployment Window file types), unity-iap (In-App Purchasing v5 call by call: store connection, the pending/confirm flow, receipts, entitlement, restore), unity-ads-levelplay (LevelPlay mediation: native dependency resolution, consent before init, rewarded/interstitial/banner units, impression-level revenue), unity-multiplayer-services (the Sessions API: join codes, a browsable game list, quick join, ticket matchmaking, relay, host migration, dedicated servers), unity-vivox (voice and text chat: sign-in, group/echo/positional channels, the roster, mute and push-to-talk, microphone permission). AI asset generation: codex-visual (2D art through the codex image model, held on-style by one art bible and one anchor — grid one-shot sets, animation sheets generated as one grid and sliced into measured frames with a GIF preview, chroma-key transparency, normalised sizes and a geometry gate that reads centre and size back from the shipped files — position and size are never asked of the model), comfyui-asset-generation (music, SFX, MiniMax H3 video and image-to-3D props through a self-hosted ComfyUI — one job at a time, /history as the only proof, /free before a model switch), blender-character-rig (an image-to-3D character rigged and animated in a running Blender through its MCP server — bones placed from measured landmarks, skin weights computed by position where bone heat fails on a double shell, an extreme-pose render as the weight test, a prop parented to a hand bone, an FK action keyed in armature axes, contact measured before a render, and an FBX read back by re-import). Install in Unity projects.
